claim: Corrected: Abrami 2015 overall g=0.30 (341 effects) is stable across subject, age and duration. The 0.57 is an OUTCOME split (content-specific CT measures, 97 effects), not content-specific teaching; explicit vs infused teaching did not differ significantly.
agent_test: Do not use K01 to justify class-keyed memory. Test directly: class-keyed vs shared lessons at equal tokens.

claim: Transfer of trained cognitive skills to distant tasks is near zero when active controls are used: Sala & Gobet music 0.03 vs 0.25 passive; WM 0.05 vs 0.18; Gobet & Sala 2023 grand mean 0.00 (332 samples).
agent_test: Compare scaffold gain on trained task family vs distant family at equal tokens, with an active-control prompt of equal length.
audit_note: Numbers match (music 0.03 active vs 0.25 passive; WM 0.05 vs 0.18; second-order grand mean 0.00 with active controls), but both sources are by the same lab (Sala and Gobet), the 2023 paper re-using their 2019 meta-analytic data; the 332 samples is the whole dataset while the 0.00 grand mean rests on the 142 active-control samples.

claim: In cognitive-training meta-analyses (Sala and Gobet), far-transfer effects shrink toward zero when active rather than passive controls are used, which points to passive-control or expectation artefacts in those literatures; by analogy, a scaffold test should include an equal-length placebo prompt.
agent_test: Run scaffold vs length-matched neutral prompt, not only vs bare prompt.
audit_note: Sala and Gobet show effects shrink with active controls in music, WM and chess training, not that 'every' far-transfer effect is partly artefact; chess had only one active-control study and the authors' conclusion is contested; the prompt-control step is a design inference, not a finding.
claim_before_audit: Part of every apparent far-transfer effect is a passive-control or expectation artefact, so any scaffold test needs an equal-length placebo prompt.

claim: Near transfer works, far transfer fails in WM training: updating-to-span g=0.176 but span-to-updating 0.048 (n.s.), 55 studies.
agent_test: Check whether lessons learned on one operator carry to its inverse.

claim: Human spontaneous analogical transfer is low without a hint and higher with one. Verified second-hand: Gick & Holyoak 1983 Exp 2 29% (8/28) vs 50% (14/28); 2025 adaptation 6.3-20.3% vs 8.7-37%. The 20-30% vs 90% pair is not verified. GPT-4 in a matching version: no hint ~0 correct-source recall, hint recall 1.00 but precision ~0.5.
agent_test: Test retrieval-with-cue vs no cue for reusing a solved source problem.
audit_note: Puranam et al. 2025 verified (humans 6.3/20.3% no hint vs 8.7/37% hint; quoting Gick and Holyoak 29% (8/28) vs 50% (14/28); GPT-4 no-hint precision/recall 0, with-hint recall 1.00, precision 0.50-0.52); Willingham text is a loose second-hand description only. Note GPT-4 'correct-source recall' is not 'solved the problem'.

claim: Thinking depends on background knowledge of the subject; both sides of the McPeck-Ennis debate accept this.
agent_test: Ablate domain facts in context vs generic reasoning instructions.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLM accuracy falls under counterfactual task variants: GPT-4 two-digit addition 100% base-10 vs 23.4% base-9 (38.6% with 0-shot CoT); GPT-3.5 drawing programs 99% to 62-75%; comprehension checks mostly passed.
agent_test: Run base-variant vs counterfactual-variant pairs with and without scaffold at equal tokens.

claim: LLM accuracy on deterministic tasks depends on how probable the text is (Embers of Autoregression, GPT-4): word reversal 97% when the answer is a high-probability sentence vs 53% when low-probability; rot-13 21% for high-probability input vs 11% for low-probability input. The same paper also reports task-frequency effects (common vs rare variants of a task).
agent_test: Report accuracy by task familiarity bucket.
audit_note: Embers numbers are right but they show sensitivity to the probability of the output or input text (GPT-4 word reversal 97% vs 53%, rot-13 21% vs 11%), not pretraining frequency of the task form; the only distinct listed source is this one paper (c25 is blank).
claim_before_audit: LLM performance tracks pretraining frequency of the task form (Embers: word reversal 97% vs 53%; rot-13 21% vs 11%).

claim: Irrelevant clauses cause large drops: GSM-NoOp up to -65.7 points (Phi-3-mini), o1-preview -17.5, o1-mini -29.1; GSM-IC <30% consistent solving.
agent_test: Add a relevance-filtering state and test on NoOp-style items.
audit_note: GSM-Symbolic Fig 8a (Phi-3-mini -65.7, o1-preview -17.5, o1-mini -29.1) and GSM-IC (fewer than 30% of base problems consistently solved) verified.

claim: Reordering premises costs 20-40+ points on deduction but only 9-15 points on R-GSM (GPT-4-turbo 94.1 to 85.0; GPT-3.5 67.3 to 51.8). Zero-shot only; no scaffold arm.
agent_test: Premise-order shuffle test with and without a restate-then-order step.

claim: CoT out-of-distribution failure: exact match 100% in distribution, 0.01% for new composition, 0% OOD in controlled small models; LLaMA3-8B composition 8.52%. Small SFT on unseen patterns patches it fast.
agent_test: Scaffold test on compositions of known steps unseen in examples.
audit_note: DataAlchemy paper (2508.01191) verified: ID 100%, CMP 0.01%, POOD/OOD 0%, LLaMA3-8B CMP 8.52%, small SFT portion generalises quickly; all figures rest on this one paper (other listed sources cover different points and were not needed).

claim: Chain-of-thought gains concentrate in maths and symbolic tasks (14.2, 12.3 points avg), near zero elsewhere (56.8 vs 56.1).
agent_test: Route: use scaffold only where CoT helps; compare to always-on at equal tokens.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external signal does not help and can hurt: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after one round; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0; oracle labels help.
agent_test: Compare self-critique with an external checker at equal tokens.

claim: RL on maths transfers to other reasoning and non-reasoning tasks, SFT often does not (non-reasoning avg base 45.7, SFT-think 21.1, RL 53.2).
agent_test: Not testable on a prompt scaffold; informs model choice only. Contested: General-Reasoner finds math-only costs about 2 points elsewhere (c11).

claim: Math-only training does not beat broad-domain training on non-math tasks (General-Reasoner).
agent_test: Model-level, not scaffold-level.

claim: Memory of workflows/experience from past tasks transfers to new tasks: AWM Mind2Web step SR cross-domain 18.6 to 32.6/35.5, cross-task 36.2 to 45.1/43.6 (GPT-4).
agent_test: Memory keyed by class vs global, at equal retrieved tokens.

claim: Memory gain does not shrink steadily with distance on web tasks: ReasoningBank SSR gain +4.6/+2.2/+4.7 (flash) and +1.2/+2.1/+3.1 (pro) for cross-task/website/domain, while AWM falls below no-memory cross-domain (30.1 vs 31.9). No reasoning-task distance curve exists.
agent_test: Measure gain by retrieval distance (same class, sibling class, other domain).

claim: Test-time curated memory lifts scores large on repeated-structure tasks: Dynamic Cheatsheet AIME24 23.3 to 50.0, AIME25 6.7 to 36.7, GPQA-D 59.6 to 68.7 (verified); GPT-4o Game of 24 10% to about 99%. Full-history baseline helps far less (26.7).
agent_test: Curated vs append-all memory at equal tokens.

claim: Curation beats raw accumulation: add-all memory lowered success vs a small fixed memory in 4 of 4 agents (RegAgent 67.5 to 55.5; AgentDriver 40.1 to 32.3; CIC-IoT 71.5 to 59.9); strict filtering raised it (70.95, 51.0, 85.4). Dynamic Cheatsheet full-history also lagged (26.7 vs 50.0).
agent_test: Add a pruning step; compare.
audit_note: Memory-management paper (add-all vs fixed: 67.53/55.48, 40.11/32.32, 71.50/59.90, plus a fourth agent 16.75/13.05; strict 70.95/51.00/85.40) and Dynamic Cheatsheet (AIME 2024, Claude, FH 26.7 vs DC 50.0) verified; the DC figure is one task and one model, and FH is still slightly above baseline 23.3.

claim: ExpeL cross-task transfer of extracted insights: FEVER Act 58, ReAct 63, transfer 65-70.
agent_test: Insights extracted on HotpotQA applied to FEVER, per class.

claim: Self-composed reasoning structures raise BBH +11% (GPT-4) with 10-40x less compute than self-consistency.
agent_test: Compare self-discover-style plan vs fixed scaffold at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs show weak far analogy: GPT-3 far story analogy p=0.065 (n.s.) while near analogy significant; humans N=54.
agent_test: Test current model on far vs near analogy with scaffold.

claim: Reasoning-model collapse past complexity is partly an evaluation artefact: Hanoi collapses coincide with output limits, some River Crossing instances (N>=6, capacity 3) are unsolvable; tools (Python) restore Hanoi to N=13. Checker Jumping stays 0 for N>=3. Evidence is thin (preliminary rebuttal; 5 trials per cell).
agent_test: Contested because puzzle-design critiques (output limits) were not read in this run.

claim: Inquiry-based learning meta-analysis reports g=1.336 but with I2=92% and funnel asymmetry (Egger p<.001); not reliable as an effect size.
agent_test: Do not use the number.

claim: Moderators in education meta-analyses: subject domain not a significant moderator (Qm=1.43, p=.698) in inquiry meta-analysis, which cuts against strong subject-specificity but rests on a biased pool.
agent_test: Check class-keyed vs shared lessons directly.

claim: Targeted instruction plus voting rescues part of the distractor loss, but not all: code-davinci-002 macro accuracy CoT 6.0, +instruction 15.0, CoT+SC 30.0, LTM+SC 45.0 (micro 72.4 to 93.4).
agent_test: Run scaffold-on vs scaffold-off on GSM-NoOp and premise-order with a frontier model.

claim: A generic instruction of the same form does not help; only the instruction naming the failure mode does (Shi et al.). That is a usable placebo arm.
agent_test: Placebo arm: same-length generic task instruction, no failure-mode content.

claim: In Wang et al. (InstructGPT, GSM8K), CoT demonstrations with invalid reasoning keep about 80-90% of CoT performance (answer accuracy 39.5 vs 48.5), while relevance-free rationales fall to 11.0 answer accuracy (intermediate-step recall 9.6 vs 43.9); incoherent-only rationales keep about half (23.1). Hence a control prompt should vary relevance and coherence separately from correctness.
agent_test: Three arms: valid scaffold, invalid-but-relevant, off-topic of equal length.
audit_note: Wang et al. (text-davinci-002, Table 2): invalid reasoning keeps 39.5/48.5 GSM8K answer accuracy (about 81%), but 9.6 vs 43.9 is intermediate-step recall, not task accuracy (answer accuracy 11.0 vs 48.5); incoherent-only prompts keep about half (23.1 vs 48.5), and Bamboogle drops far less; single model setting. Min et al. (random labels) does not bear on scaffold relevance.
claim_before_audit: Wrong-but-relevant scaffolds keep 80-90% of CoT's gain; irrelevant or incoherent ones destroy it (9.6 vs 43.9). So the control must vary relevance, not correctness.

claim: Filler tokens give compute benefit only in small trained models; no evidence that prompted frontier models gain from filler.
agent_test: Optional floor arm only.

claim: Unfiltered memory accumulation hurts and agents copy the nearest stored record (experience-following); history-based deletion by downstream utility helps only with a reliable judge.
agent_test: Admit a lesson only after a verifier passes; delete lessons whose retrievals lead to failures.

claim: Topic-keyed vs shared memory at equal retrieved tokens has no direct test; Dynamic Cheatsheet lists it as future work, and reasoning models (R1, o1) gained little from DC.
agent_test: Run keyed vs shared pool, same token budget, held-out by class.

claim: Compositionality gap: ~40% of 2-hop questions with both sub-answers known are wrong; self-ask with search lifts 2Wiki EM 25.4 to 40.1 (davinci-002). Not tested on current reasoning models.
agent_test: Test explicit decomposition into known sub-steps on a frontier model with tools.

claim: Tool use (Python) rescues rule-driven long-procedure puzzles for reasoning models; unsolvable-by-design cases remain unsolved.
agent_test: Give the agent a code-execution operator before declaring a complexity limit.

claim: Abrami moderator-adjusted question stays unresolved: the primary paper was blocked (403); summary says stage 1 screened by design type and instrument.
agent_test: Obtain the full text before citing control-type effects.
